title: Care Center Training on Reconsideration of Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan Claim Decisions
content:
These questions are answered from the reconsideration terms of the Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan.

**What can be reconsidered, and how often?**
A tenant may ask once — 1 reconsideration per claim — for reconsideration of a denial or a partial approval, by supplying a document that was not on file at the first decision.

**How is the reconsideration window counted?**
The window counts calendar days starting the day after the decision date, and the last counted day is included. With a hypothetical window of 30 days and a decision on day 0, day 30 is the last day of the window.

**What happens to the earlier decision and payment?**
The new decision replaces the earlier one; any increase over the amount already paid is paid as a new claim payment, and the earlier payment stands.

*Illustration (hypothetical):* a partial approval of 1,240.00 was paid. On reconsideration the whole amount now approved is 1,790.00. The earlier payment of 1,240.00 stands, and 550.00 is paid as a new claim payment.

**What if the tenant disagrees with the assessed value but has no new document?**
A disagreement about the assessed actual cash value itself, without a new document, is not reconsidered by the care center.

| Request | Reconsidered by the care center? |
| --- | --- |
| denial or partial approval, new document not on file at the first decision, first request | yes |
| a second request on the same claim | no |
| disagreement with the assessed value, no new document | no |

**Former window clause.** The former clause that a reconsideration is taken only when requested not later than the decision date plus the level's reconsideration window is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

superseded_clauses: A reconsideration is taken only when it is requested not later than the decision date plus claim_reconsideration_window_days.
